title: Product Roadmap & Sprint Planning (Q3)
summary: The product and engineering leadership aligned on major Q3 goals, prioritizing the mobile app redesign, API v2 specifications, and search latency improvements. Elena showcased interactive prototypes for the navigation overhaul, which received positive feedback. Alex highlighted backend database optimizations required to maintain sub-100ms transcript queries. Action items were distributed across UI design, backend benchmarking, and API documentation.

action_items.text: Finalize mobile navigation wireframes in Figma
Benchmark SQLite query execution under high concurrency
Draft API v2 migration guide for frontend team
Publish sprint goals on the company Notion wiki
Schedule weekly UX review with stakeholders

raw_transcript:
[00:00:00] Sarah Chen: Good afternoon everyone. Let's get started with our Q3 roadmap and sprint kickoff.
[00:00:25] Alex Rivera: Thanks Sarah. On the backend side, our priority is supporting high volume transcription queries with zero stutter.
[00:00:58] Dev Patel: From the frontend perspective, we want the player seeking and transcript highlight loop to be completely instantaneous.
[00:01:35] Elena Rostova: I've also completed the initial design pass on the meeting detail layout, including the player sync controls.
[00:02:10] Sarah Chen: Fantastic. Can we first look at the overall objectives before we dive into individual sprint tickets?
[00:03:00] Alex Rivera: Absolutely. Our primary metric is keeping API response times under 50ms for meeting listings and search.
[00:03:45] Dev Patel: We should also make sure our TanStack Query cache invalidations are rock-solid whenever meetings are updated.
[00:04:40] Elena Rostova: Moving to section two: the mobile navigation. I've prepared three variations for the responsive drawer and tabs.
[00:05:30] Sarah Chen: I prefer option B because it preserves vertical space for the transcript reader on smaller screens.
[00:06:15] Elena Rostova: Makes sense. I'll refine the Figma tokens accordingly and share the export by Wednesday.
[00:07:00] Dev Patel: That works well for me. I can start building the presentation components right after.
[00:08:00] Alex Rivera: Next on our agenda is performance. We noticed full-text searches on large transcripts need proper composite indexing.
[00:08:50] Sarah Chen: Does the current SQLite schema with cascade deletion handle concurrent read operations smoothly?
[00:09:40] Alex Rivera: Yes, with WAL mode and proper foreign key pragmas, it handles our intended workload easily.
[00:10:30] Dev Patel: Are we still introducing the new /api/v1/meetings endpoints this week?
[00:11:15] Alex Rivera: Yes, the REST endpoints are completely versioned and match the OpenAPI contract exactly.
[00:12:00] Sarah Chen: Excellent. Let's make sure the action item toggle and delete endpoints have full integration test coverage.
[00:12:45] Dev Patel: I'll also add optimistic updates in the client so checkboxes flip with immediate visual feedback.
[00:13:30] Elena Rostova: Please ensure the completed items have clear strikethrough styling and accessible contrast ratios.
[00:14:15] Sarah Chen: Let's summarize our action items and wrap up on time. Elena, wireframes; Alex, benchmark tests; Dev, API guide.
[00:15:00] Alex Rivera: Sounds like a solid plan. Thanks team!
[00:15:30] Dev Patel: Talk to you all at tomorrow's standup.
[00:16:00] Elena Rostova: Goodbye everyone!

title: Weekly Engineering Standup & Tech Debt Review
summary: Engineering team held their recurring technical sync to address platform reliability and continuous integration bottlenecks. Marcus reported on GitHub Actions cache improvements that cut test run times in half. Alex shared findings on SQLite indexing strategies for transcript segments. Dev reviewed progress on migrating query state to TanStack Query hooks.

topics.title: Flaky CI Pipeline Resolution & Docker Caching

action_items.text: Add composite index on transcript segments table
Investigate GitHub Actions test timeout issue
Upgrade React Query to TanStack Query v5 in web repo

raw_transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Rivera: Morning everyone. Quick standup today, followed by tech debt updates.
[00:00:30] Marcus Vance: Good morning. On my side, CI builds were failing intermittently due to apt mirror timeouts.
[00:01:10] Dev Patel: I noticed that on the PR builds yesterday. Glad you caught it.
[00:01:45] Marcus Vance: I switched us to pinned Ubuntu mirrors and enabled GitHub Actions layer caching. Run time dropped from 8 minutes to 3.5 minutes.
[00:02:30] Alex Rivera: That's a huge win for team productivity. How about local test execution?
[00:03:10] Dev Patel: Local pytest runs finish in under two seconds using our in-memory SQLite fixtures.
[00:04:00] Alex Rivera: Regarding tech debt: I added composite indexes on (meeting_id, sequence_index) to speed up sequential segment reads.
[00:04:55] Dev Patel: That directly helps the transcript viewer render without layout thrashing.
[00:05:40] Marcus Vance: Are there any migration scripts required for developers pulling main?
[00:06:20] Alex Rivera: None at all. Base.metadata.create_all handles table initialization and foreign keys are verified on connect.
[00:07:15] Dev Patel: Awesome. I'll finish up the action item complete toggle endpoint today.
[00:08:00] Alex Rivera: Perfect. Keep up the great work everyone.

Complete GDPR security review for EU data residency
Prepare sales enablement pitch deck for enterprise sales team

Coordinate co-marketing webinar with strategic partners

title: Quick 1-on-1 Design Sync: Component Styling
